correctness.rationale: Write S=2(1+rho^2). In the conditional squared norm, multiplying the cross term by the entry-square sampling weight and summing over j yields −2 alpha ||Ax||^2/S; the squared update yields 2 alpha^2 ||Ax||^2/S because both entries in each row are nonzero. The least singular value 1−rho gives the stated theta in (0,1), and iteration, Jensen for orders at most two, and summable Markov bounds followed by Borel–Cantelli establish all the decay assertions. For the two rare choices of weight rho^2/S each, the updated coordinates jointly form W x with W having diagonal 1−alpha and off-diagonal −alpha/rho. The conditional pth moment is at least (rho^2/S) 2^(1−p/2) ||W x||^p. For rho<alpha/(1−alpha) the least singular value is alpha/rho−(1−alpha), giving exactly L_p and a uniform-in-state lower bound at each step. For fixed p>2, L_p tends to infinity as rho tends to zero, while rho<epsilon/(2+epsilon) enforces the strict condition-number bound. This verifies the quantifier order and finite-time finiteness (four finite update matrices). Independent exact arithmetic gave 11/9, 323/404, and 6561/6464 and checked the quadratic-form identity at the rational example on the two basis vectors and their sum.
residual_risks: The rational replay is finite; the analytic bounds establish the all-time and real-order conclusions. Divergence is asserted for the selected sufficiently small rho, not for every rho and not simultaneously for all p>2 at one rho.

value.rationale: The example identifies the threshold order across solver instances: mean-square convergence and almost-sure convergence coexist with arbitrarily fast pth-moment growth for any requested order above two, even when the SPD matrix is arbitrarily close to the identity. This rules out a condition-number-based inference of tail or moment control for this sampling scheme and isolates the concrete cause, rare division by tiny entries, uniformly over initial directions.
residual_risks: This is an exact-arithmetic counterexample with no claim on safeguarded or finite-precision implementations, or on exact pth-moment growth rates.
